messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated 95th percentile latency and SSE connection failures detected in us-west-2 between 22:03-22:05 UTC. Affected route: /v1/chat/stream. Error spike -> connection reset / 502s. Auto-escalation to #incidents.

alex_k: I'm on it. Paging SRE on-call. Can someone confirm whether this is capacity or a code-level regression?

maria_p: Looking at runtime metrics now — token processing latency per-GPU is steady, but we see a large increase in open SSE connections and a backlog in the muxer. Seems like downstream backpressure (clients) + slight auth-service flakiness.

samir: Support: a handful of heavy customers reported partial stream truncation around 22:03. They're hitting streaming for long-lived responses (chat + tool calls).

anya: Product: if we need to kill streaming temporarily, what's the customer impact surface? We should prepare comms.

ryan_eng: Decision node: prefer soft mitigation first — shift heavy clients to non-streaming (polling) and rate-limit new streaming starts. If that fails, flip stream off for the region. I can execute a controlled disable.

maria_p: Agreed. We can do a targeted toggle by region and by plan. Patch config via control-plane feature-flag API. Example command:

```
# disable streaming for us-west-2 only
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/feature-flags/streaming \
  -d '{"region":"us-west-2","enabled":false,"note":"incident 2234567890 - temporary disable"}'
```

alex_k: @ryan_eng you're on handoff for the mitigation. @maria_p and @samir coordinate customer impact and support routing. I'll keep the page open.

samir: Support note: Recommend increasing poll window/short-poll rate limit for affected customers so their UX degrades gracefully. We can white-list a small set of enterprise clients for manual handing if needed.

maria_p: Also toggling a soft rate cap on streaming starts to prevent connection storms. Command snippet:

```
# set max concurrent new streaming connections per tenant
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/tenants/streaming-limits \
  -d '{"region":"us-west-2","new_stream_rate":20}'
```

ryan_eng: Executing the rate-cap now. Will watch for 5m. If error rate doesn't improve, I'll flip the streaming flag off.

incident-bot: Action recorded: rate cap change applied by ryan_eng at 22:07:14 UTC.

maria_p: Watching muxer queue — backlog decreased ~40% after rate cap. Latency trending down but SSE error rate still elevated for long-lived streams.

samir: Customer-facing note draft (for support/ops): "We're experiencing degraded streaming performance in us-west-2. We're temporarily limiting new streaming sessions and may disable streaming briefly to stabilize service. Polling endpoints remain available. We'll update shortly." Thoughts?

anya: Add: guidance for devs to switch to generate/poll endpoints and a link to the status page. Keep it short.

ryan_eng: 22:12:30 UTC — going to disable streaming for us-west-2. Will leave a short window open to rollback if errors spike. Command:

```
# atomic regional streaming disable
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/feature-flags/streaming/disable \
  -d '{"region":"us-west-2","reason":"mitigation - high SSE error spike","expires_in_min":30}'
```

alex_k: Please also push a temporary rate limit increase on the non-streaming endpoints so clients can poll without overwhelming the backend.

maria_p: Done. Non-streaming token-generation quota increased by 2x for us-west-2 for 30m.

incident-bot: Action recorded: streaming disabled for region us-west-2 by ryan_eng at 22:13:05 UTC.

samir: Sending support broadcast now to impacted customer contacts with suggested mitigation steps and ETA ~30m. (CC @anya for comms)

support-bot: Broadcast sent to 12 enterprise contacts.

maria_p: Post-disable check: SSE errors dropped to baseline within 90s, muxer backlog drained, overall 95th latency down ~600ms. No new increases in CPU/GPU.

anya: Great. Drafting status page update: "We identified elevated SSE connection failures; streaming responses have been temporarily disabled in us-west-2 while we stabilize. Non-streaming endpoints remain available. We expect streaming to return within 30 minutes pending monitoring".

ryan_eng: Monitoring tail logs and metrics for next 15m. Rollback criteria: SSE error rate < 0.5% for 10m, muxer queue < 5 for 10m, no new downstream auth errors. Roll-forward criteria: if overall latencies creep up or error rate worsens, keep disable.

alex_k: Incident note: document timeline + commands used (rate cap, feature-flag disable) and create postmortem stub. Assign to eng-runtime and oncall SRE.

maria_p: Will capture a thread with graphs and the flag toggles.

samir: Support follow-up: most affected customers saw seamless failover to polling; two customers reported minor UX issues (missing partial stream fragments) — logged cases and assigned severity 2.

incident-bot: Metric alert cleared for SSE error spike at 22:24:50 UTC.

ryan_eng: Re-enabling streaming will be a controlled canary: enable for 5% of traffic -> monitor 10m -> 25% -> monitor -> full. We'll coordinate next steps in this thread before flipping.

anya: I'll prepare a short FAQ for customers about the temporary change and steps to update clients if they want to proactively switch to polling.

alex_k: Nice work team. Keep updates here. I'll close the page once postmortem is created and customers are updated. :white_check_mark:
